expectations.evidence: Lists HEMMELIG, STRENGT HEMMELIG, KONFIDENSIELT, and BEGRENSET in glossary but never mentions UGRADERT. Missing one of the five required levels.
Section 2.1 extensively references Sikkerhetsloven (Lov om nasjonal sikkerhet, 2018) as governing framework with specific chapter references (Ch. 5-9).
NSM identified as 'Nasjonal sikkerhetsmyndighet -- Norwegian National Security Authority' with specific role as accreditation authority (section 1, 2.2, and throughout).

Section 2.2 references 'Grunnprinsipper for IKT-sikkerhet' as NSM's foundational security principles with four categories (identify, protect, detect, respond). Compliance matrix in 2.4 maps requirements to specific Grunnprinsipper. Listed as primary baseline.

Section 8.5 specifies 'NSM-approved national cryptographic products' for data at rest and internal transport, distinct from NATO crypto. Section 2.4 compliance matrix states 'NSM-approved crypto (national)'. HSMs must be on NSM's approved list (section 6.3).

Section 7.1 details the 8-person HEMMELIG klarering constraint with role breakdown, separation of duties, and explicit acknowledgment that 'With only 8 cleared personnel, some role overlap is unavoidable.' Klareringsforskriften referenced in section 2.1.
Dedicated section 8 covers NATO interop: FMN Spiral 5 compliance, STANAG 4774/4778 for classification marking, NATO-approved Type 1 crypto for NATO SECRET, and CDS-mediated data sharing.

Section 5.4 details NSM-accredited CDS for NATO interoperability with bidirectional filtered exchange. Section 5.3 covers data diode for BEGRENSET-to-HEMMELIG transfers. Clear separation between national and NATO crypto domains at CDS boundary (section 8.5).

Section 13.2 dedicated to TEMPEST requirements for HEMMELIG: NSM TEMPEST authority assessment, Zone 1/2 equipment requirements, fiber optic cabling preference, and TEMPEST measurements as part of accreditation.
Section 9.1 explicitly states 'All HEMMELIG data must remain on Norwegian sovereign territory at all times' with no foreign replication/backup and physical location requirements in Norway.
No mention of NIS2, EEA, or GDPR anywhere in the document.

While NSM Grunnprinsipper is primary baseline, the document references DISA STIG and CIS benchmarks for hardening (line 193: 'extensive hardening guides (DISA STIG, CIS)' and line 926: 'Apply CIS/DISA STIG benchmarks to all systems'), and FIPS-validated crypto modules. US standards are used alongside Norwegian ones rather than Norwegian standards being clearly primary for hardening.
